newsitem.title: JAPAN: Busang impact on gold muted, Indon mining to be hit.
newsitem.headline: Busang impact on gold muted, Indon mining to be hit.

text.p: Asian gold markets shrugged off news that the Busang gold find in Indonesia was not nearly as rich as reported, but dealers expressed fears about its possible impact on the country's lucrative mining programme.

Spot gold in Tokyo was seen at US$349.75/$350.15 an ounce while Hong Kong dealers used the news as an excuse for shortcovering to push spot gold prices to $350.10/60 an ounce, unchanged from New York's overnight close.
"The immediate impact on the gold price will be muted," said Koichiro Kamei, manager of information and planning for the World Gold Council's (WGC) Japan office.
"The impact from the Bre-X News on the gold price would be rather short-lived, as the market was looking for a factor to cover shorts," a trader at a major trading house in Tokyo said.

"The news triggered speculative interest in gold in New York overnight. But it is unlikely to have a significant impact on the world demand/supply factor since there are other major gold suppliers," he said.
Hong Kong dealers said gold sales by central banks or by the International Monetary Fund tended to cast a much more serious shadow over gold prices.
"I don't expect gold to shoot up $20 an ounce," one gold trader said.
Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd said in February that gold reserves in Busang on Borneo island were estimated at nearly 71 million ounces in what was hailed as the century's biggest find.
The announcement by Bre-X on Wednesday that there was a "strong possibility" the potential reserves were overstated prompted a halt in trading in the company's shares in the Toronto Stock Exchange.
But the Asian gold trade was more concerned about the possible setback to Indonesia's mining industry and its gold production programme.
Indonesia is seen by mining industry experts as the best place to do business in Asia and this image may be dented by Busang.

"Any Indonesian exploration company is being valued based on its location relative to Busang," said Aaron Colleran, an analyst for stockbrokers Eyres Reed Ltd. He said a number of Canadian companies were in this category.

"People in the trade are more concerned about how the Indonesian government would react to this. In the long run, it may affect Indonesia's gold production and exploration programme," a senior gold dealer for a Singapore bank said.
"It's incredible that something like this could have happened," another Singapore-based dealer said.
The fallout in Bre-X immediately took its toll in Australia on peripheral Busang player Golden Valley Mines, whose shares immediately lost ground.

Golden Valley has a technical and financial agreement with Indonesian company PT Krueng Gasui (KG), controlled by businessman Joseph Merukh. KG owns an undisputed 10 percent stake in the Muara Atan contract of work containing part of the Busang deposit.

"There could be a problem from financial sides in the project, as share prices will slump following the B-X news. As a result, it is highly likely that the development of the mining project will be delayed," Kamei said.
